# Vehicle Seat with Enhanced Luggage Storage Utilizing Tip-Up Function

## Background and Objective

In vehicles equipped with foldable or tip-up seating systems, a significant amount of space is often created beneath and around the seat cushion when it is rotated into its upright, tipped-up position. However, conventional vehicle seat designs frequently fail to make efficient use of this vacant space, resulting in underutilized storage potential. The present invention addresses this shortcoming by providing a vehicle seat structure specifically designed to effectively utilize the space created when the seat cushion is tipped up, thereby maximizing the available luggage storage capacity within the vehicle interior. This is achieved through a novel arrangement of support components and a slide mechanism that work in concert to optimize spatial efficiency without compromising the structural integrity or functionality of the seat.

## Structural Configuration

The vehicle seat according to the present invention comprises several key structural elements that work together to achieve the stated objective. First, the seat includes a **support leg** configured to bear and transmit the weight and load associated with the seat cushion, ensuring that the cushion remains properly supported during normal seating use. Second, a **leg holding member** is provided to securely hold and retain the lower portion of the support leg, thereby maintaining the structural stability of the seat cushion assembly. Third, the seat is equipped with a **slide mechanism** that enables the seat cushion and seat back to move together in the front/back (fore-aft) direction, allowing the overall seat position to be adjusted according to the needs of the vehicle occupants or the storage requirements at any given time.

## Tip-Up Function

A defining feature of this vehicle seat is its **tip-up function**, which allows the seat cushion to be rotated such that its front part becomes elevated relative to its rear part. As the seat cushion rotates through this motion, the seating surface—normally oriented upward to support an occupant—comes to face the front surface of the seat back. In other words, when the tip-up function is engaged, the seat cushion pivots upward and rotates so that its seating surface and the seat back's front surface confront one another, effectively folding the seat cushion against the seat back. This configuration creates the vacant space beneath and around the seat cushion that can then be utilized for storing luggage or other cargo items, addressing the core objective of the invention.

## Integration of Leg Holding Member with Slide Mechanism

A particularly advantageous aspect of this invention lies in the positioning of the leg holding member relative to the slide mechanism. Specifically, the leg holding member is disposed at a portion of the slide mechanism that moves synchronously with the seat cushion and seat back. This integrated arrangement ensures that as the seat cushion and seat back are adjusted along the front/back direction via the slide mechanism, the leg holding member—and by extension, the support leg it retains—moves in tandem with these components. 

This design offers several benefits: it eliminates the need for a separate, independently operating support structure for the leg holding member, thereby simplifying the overall seat assembly and reducing the number of components required. Furthermore, by integrating the leg holding member directly with the movable portion of the slide mechanism, the invention ensures consistent and reliable support for the seat cushion regardless of its position along the slide, while simultaneously preserving the vacant space created during the tip-up operation for maximum storage utility. This cohesive integration of the support structure with the seat's movable components represents a key innovation that enhances both the functionality and the space efficiency of the vehicle seat.

# Vehicle Seat with Tip-Up Cushion and Sliding Leg Support Mechanism

## Background of the Invention

In many vehicles, particularly those with rear or auxiliary seating positions, seat cushions are designed to tip up in order to create additional space within the vehicle cabin. This tip-up functionality is commonly used to accommodate tall or bulky cargo, bicycles, or other items that would not otherwise fit when the seat is in its normal, occupant-ready position. However, a persistent challenge in the design of such seats has been the inefficient use of the space that becomes available beneath and around the seat cushion once it has been tipped up. Conventional seat structures often leave this space underutilized because the support legs, which normally bear the weight of the seat cushion and its occupant, remain fixed in position or interfere with the newly created void, thereby limiting the practical storage potential of the tipped-up configuration.

Additionally, traditional seat assemblies typically restrict movement to a single rotational tip-up action, without providing complementary front-to-back sliding capability. This lack of coordinated movement between rotation and translation significantly limits the adaptability of the seat system, preventing users from fully customizing the interior layout to suit varying cargo sizes and shapes.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these shortcomings by providing a vehicle seat assembly that integrates three key structural elements—a support leg, a leg holding member, and a slide mechanism—which work in concert to enable both rotational tip-up movement and front/back sliding movement of the seat cushion and seat back. This combined functionality allows the vacant space created when the seat cushion is tipped up to be effectively transformed into usable luggage or cargo storage space, thereby significantly enhancing the practicality and versatility of the vehicle seat.

## Detailed Description of the Components and Their Interaction

**Support Leg**

The support leg serves as the primary structural member that supports the seat cushion and, by extension, the seat back, when the seat is in its normal, deployed position for occupant use. The support leg is designed to bear the load of a seated passenger while also being configured to permit the seat cushion to rotate upward into a tipped-up position when the seat is not in use for seating purposes.

**Leg Holding Member**

A critical innovation of this invention lies in the leg holding member, which is responsible for retaining and positioning the support leg. Rather than being fixed to a stationary part of the vehicle floor or seat frame, the leg holding member is mounted on the moving part of the slide mechanism. This strategic placement allows the leg holding member—and consequently the support leg itself—to move along with the sliding action of the seat assembly. As a result, when the seat cushion is tipped up, the support leg is not confined to a single fixed location but can instead be repositioned along the front/back axis of the vehicle, depending on the sliding position selected by the user.

**Slide Mechanism**

The slide mechanism provides the means by which the entire seat assembly, including the leg holding member and support leg, can be moved in the front and back direction relative to the vehicle floor. The slide mechanism consists of a fixed rail portion, which is anchored to the vehicle floor, and a moving part that travels along this fixed rail. By mounting the leg holding member directly onto this moving part, the invention ensures that the support leg's position is dynamically linked to the overall sliding position of the seat.

## Operation and Advantages

When the seat is in its normal position, the support leg, held securely in place by the leg holding member, provides stable support for the seat cushion beneath a seated occupant. The slide mechanism, in this configuration, allows the user to adjust the fore-and-aft position of the seat for comfort and legroom, as is typical in adjustable vehicle seating.

When additional cargo space is required, the seat cushion can be rotated upward into its tipped-up position. Because the leg holding member is mounted on the sliding portion of the slide mechanism, the support leg can be moved forward or backward along with the seat cushion and seat back assembly. This coordinated movement allows the user to reposition the support leg out of the way of the newly created storage void, or to adjust its position to optimize the available space for a particular item of luggage or cargo.

This combination of rotational tip-up movement and translational front/back sliding movement represents a significant improvement over conventional designs, in which the support leg remains fixed and often obstructs or limits the usable volume of the tipped-up space. By allowing the leg holding member—and thus the support leg—to travel with the slide mechanism, the invention maximizes the flexibility of the vacant space, effectively converting it into a more accessible and functional luggage compartment.

## Conclusion

Through the synergistic combination of a support leg, a leg holding member mounted on the moving part of a slide mechanism, and the slide mechanism itself, this invention successfully addresses the longstanding challenge of underutilized space in tip-up vehicle seat designs. The resulting seat assembly not only retains full functionality for normal seating use, including adjustable fore-and-aft positioning, but also transforms into a versatile and space-efficient cargo storage solution when the seat cushion is tipped up. This innovation enhances the overall practicality, convenience, and versatility of vehicle interior space management, providing significant benefits to vehicle manufacturers and end users alike.

# The Word "The"

The word "the" is one of the most fascinating elements of the English language, despite—or perhaps because of—its apparent simplicity. As the most frequently used word in English, "the" appears in written and spoken language more often than any other word, yet most native speakers rarely think about it.

"The" is what linguists call a definite article. Its primary function is to indicate that a noun refers to something specific or already known to the listener or reader. When we say "the dog" rather than "a dog," we signal that we're talking about a particular dog—perhaps one mentioned earlier in conversation, or one that's obviously identifiable from context.

This small word carries surprising grammatical weight. It helps distinguish between general and specific references: "I like cake" (cake in general) versus "I like the cake" (a specific cake we both know about). This distinction, while seemingly minor, is crucial for clear communication and can completely change the meaning of a sentence.

Interestingly, not all languages have a direct equivalent to "the." Russian, Chinese, and Japanese, for example, don't use articles in the same way English does, which often poses challenges for speakers of these languages when learning English. Conversely, English speakers learning languages with more complex article systems—such as German, which has different forms depending on gender and case—often struggle with mastering these nuances.

The etymology of "the" traces back to Old English, where it derived from demonstrative pronouns meaning "that" or "this." Over centuries, it evolved into the neutral, all-purpose definite article we use today, losing the gender and case distinctions that characterized its ancestors.

Despite its unassuming appearance, "the" plays an outsized role in shaping meaning, clarity, and precision in English. It reminds us that even the smallest words can carry significant linguistic and communicative power.

# OBJECT OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a vehicle seat assembly, and more particularly to a vehicle seat incorporating a tip-up cushion mechanism in combination with a foldable support leg and slide rail assembly, enabling the seat to be reconfigured between a normal seating position, a tip-up storage position, and a folded/stowed position for the purpose of maximizing cargo space and improving vehicle interior versatility.

It is an object of the present invention to provide a vehicle seat assembly that allows the seat cushion to be pivoted upward relative to the seat back into a substantially vertical tip-up position, thereby exposing a floor storage region beneath the seat.

It is a further object of the present invention to provide a support leg mechanism operatively connected to the seat cushion frame, wherein the support leg is configured to automatically fold or retract in coordinated response to the tip-up motion of the seat cushion, and to extend and lock into a floor-engaging position when the seat cushion is returned to its normal seating position.

It is another object of the present invention to provide a slide mechanism permitting fore-aft translation of the seat assembly along a pair of slide rails secured to the vehicle floor, such that the seat may be selectively positioned longitudinally within the vehicle independent of, or in combination with, the tip-up and fold-flat functions.

It is yet another object of the present invention to provide a seat assembly wherein the seat back is foldable forward onto the tipped-up or normally positioned seat cushion, allowing the entire seat assembly to collapse into a compact, low-profile configuration for flat-load cargo applications.

It is still another object of the present invention to provide a locking and release mechanism that ensures the support leg is securely locked in its extended, floor-engaging position during normal vehicle operation, while permitting single-action or minimal-effort release for reconfiguration by the vehicle occupant.

It is a further object of the present invention to provide a seat assembly of simplified construction, reduced part count, and improved structural rigidity, which may be manufactured economically and integrated readily into existing vehicle floor and seat mounting architectures.

Other objects and advantages of the present invention will become apparent from the following description, taken in connection with the accompanying drawings, wherein by way of illustration and example, an embodiment of the present invention is disclosed.

---

# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with the objects set forth above, the present invention provides a vehicle seat assembly comprising a seat back, a seat cushion pivotally connected to the seat back, a support leg assembly, and a slide mechanism for mounting the seat assembly to a vehicle floor.

The seat cushion is pivotally mounted at a forward or rearward region thereof so as to be rotatable between a generally horizontal, occupant-supporting position and a tipped-up, generally vertical position. A support leg assembly is connected to the seat cushion frame, the support leg assembly comprising at least one leg member movable between an extended position, in which the leg member engages the vehicle floor to support the seat cushion in its normal horizontal position, and a retracted or folded position, in which the leg member is displaced away from the floor to permit tipping of the seat cushion and/or forward translation of the seat assembly along the slide mechanism.

The support leg assembly is operatively linked to the seat cushion, such as through a link arm, cam surface, or bracket arrangement, such that pivotal movement of the seat cushion toward its tip-up position automatically actuates the support leg assembly toward its retracted position, and such that return movement of the seat cushion toward its normal position automatically actuates the support leg assembly toward its extended, locked position. A locking mechanism is provided to releasably retain the support leg assembly in the extended position during normal seating use, and to release the support leg assembly in response to actuation of a release handle or lever associated with the tip-up function.

The slide mechanism comprises a pair of laterally spaced slide rails adapted for fixed attachment to the vehicle floor, and a corresponding pair of slide members affixed to the seat assembly and slidably engaged with the slide rails, permitting fore-aft adjustment of the seat assembly along the vehicle floor. The slide mechanism may further include a locking device for selectively fixing the longitudinal position of the seat assembly relative to the slide rails.

In one aspect of the invention, the seat back is further pivotable relative to the seat cushion between an upright position and a forward-folded position overlying the seat cushion, such that when the seat cushion is disposed in its tip-up position and/or the support leg assembly is in its retracted position, the seat assembly as a whole may be folded and/or translated to present a substantially flat, unobstructed cargo floor surface.

The vehicle seat assembly of the present invention thereby provides a mechanically coordinated, easy-to-operate reconfiguration system that enhances cargo versatility, reduces the number of independent operator actions required to stow the seat, and maintains structural integrity and occupant safety during normal vehicle operation. Additional features, aspects, and advantages of the invention will be more fully understood from the detailed description and accompanying drawings that follow.

# VEHICLE SEAT WITH TILT-UP CUSHION LUGGAGE STORAGE ASSEMBLY

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to vehicle seat assemblies, and more particularly to a vehicle seat construction wherein a seat cushion is configured to tilt upward from a normal seating position to expose a storage compartment therebeneath, the assembly incorporating a support leg arrangement and a slide mechanism for facilitating stable positioning of the seat cushion in both the seating position and the tilted, storage-accessible position.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

In vehicle interiors, particularly in multi-purpose vehicles, vans, and passenger automobiles, space utilization is a significant design consideration. It is known in the art to provide storage compartments beneath vehicle seat cushions; however, conventional arrangements often suffer from inadequate support structures when the seat cushion is displaced to access the underlying storage space, resulting in instability of the tilted cushion, difficulty of operation, and potential damage to the seat mounting structure over repeated use. There exists a need for a vehicle seat assembly that provides reliable, stable support for a seat cushion in a tilted, storage-access configuration while maintaining structural integrity and ease of operation for the vehicle occupant.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

According to an aspect of the present invention, there is provided a vehicle seat assembly comprising a seat cushion mounted for movement between a first position, in which the seat cushion is disposed substantially horizontally to define a seating surface, and a second position, in which the seat cushion is tilted upward relative to the first position so as to expose a storage space disposed beneath the seat cushion.

The seat assembly further comprises a plurality of support legs, including a first support leg, a second support leg, and a third support leg, which support legs are configured to engage a floor of the vehicle and to support the seat cushion in at least the first position. A leg holding member is provided for retaining at least one of the support legs in a predetermined relationship relative to the seat cushion, and further for permitting relative displacement of at least one support leg upon movement of the seat cushion between the first position and the second position.

The seat assembly further comprises a slide mechanism, including a first slide member and a second slide member, disposed in operative association with the support legs and the seat cushion, whereby movement of the seat cushion from the first position toward the second position causes the slide mechanism to guide displacement of at least one of the support legs relative to the leg holding member, thereby permitting the seat cushion to tilt upward while maintaining structural support of the seat cushion assembly at least at one location proximate the vehicle floor.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals designate corresponding parts throughout the several views, there is shown a vehicle seat assembly, generally designated 1, embodying the principles of the present invention.

### General Configuration

The vehicle seat assembly 1 comprises a seat cushion 2 having an upper surface 2a configured to receive an occupant thereon when the seat cushion 2 is disposed in a first, seating position, as illustrated. The seat cushion 2 further comprises a lower surface 2b, opposite the upper surface 2a, which lower surface 2b, together with a floor panel F of the vehicle, at least partially defines a storage compartment S when the seat cushion 2 is disposed in a second, tilted position, as will be described in greater detail below.

The seat cushion 2 is preferably supported at a rearward portion thereof by a seat back assembly (not shown in detail, but of a construction known in the art), the seat back assembly being pivotally or fixedly mounted relative to the vehicle floor F. The forward portion of the seat cushion 2 is supported by the support leg arrangement described hereinbelow, such that the seat cushion 2 may be selectively pivoted or displaced about a rearward region thereof to access the storage compartment S.

### Support Leg Arrangement

The support leg arrangement comprises a first support leg 6A, a second support leg 6B, and a third support leg 6C, each of the support legs 6A, 6B, 6C extending generally between the seat cushion 2 and the vehicle floor F so as to support the seat cushion 2 in the first position at a predetermined height above the floor F.

In the preferred embodiment, the first support leg 6A and the second support leg 6B are disposed in a laterally spaced relationship relative to one another, proximate a forward portion of the seat cushion 2, whereas the third support leg 6C is disposed rearwardly of the first support leg 6A and the second support leg 6B, or alternatively at a central location, according to the particular seat configuration desired. Each of the support legs 6A, 6B, 6C preferably comprises an elongate rigid member formed of metal or a suitably rigid polymeric material, and each is provided at a lower end thereof with a floor-engaging portion configured to engage the vehicle floor F, whether directly or via a floor-mounted bracket or striker assembly affixed thereto.

At least one of the support legs, for example the third support leg 6C, is configured for displacement relative to the seat cushion 2 upon movement of the seat cushion 2 between the first position and the second position, as will be described further in connection with the leg holding member 8 and the slide mechanism 18A, 18B.

### Leg Holding Member

The seat assembly 1 further comprises a leg holding member 8 mounted to the seat cushion 2, preferably to a frame member disposed within or beneath the seat cushion 2. The leg holding member 8 is configured to retain the third support leg 6C, and optionally one or both of the first support leg 6A and second support leg 6B, in a predetermined orientation relative to the seat cushion 2 when the seat cushion 2 is disposed in the first position.

The leg holding member 8 preferably comprises a bracket having an aperture, slot, or channel formed therein, the aperture, slot, or channel being configured to receive a portion of the third support leg 6C therethrough, such that the third support leg 6C is permitted to slide, rotate, or otherwise displace relative to the leg holding member 8 as the seat cushion 2 is moved toward the second position. In this manner, the leg holding member 8 functions both to maintain the third support leg 6C in proper alignment during normal use of the seat assembly 1 in the first position, and to guide the third support leg 6C during transition of the seat cushion 2 to the second position, thereby preventing misalignment, binding, or inadvertent disengagement of the third support leg 6C from the vehicle floor F.

In an alternative embodiment, the leg holding member 8 may further comprise a biasing element, such as a spring, configured to urge the third support leg 6C toward a predetermined position relative to the leg holding member 8, thereby facilitating automatic return of the third support leg 6C to its original orientation upon return movement of the seat cushion 2 from the second position to the first position.

### Slide Mechanism

The seat assembly 1 further comprises a slide mechanism including a first slide member 18A and a second slide member 18B, the first slide member 18A and second slide member 18B being disposed in operative association with the first support leg 6A and the second support leg 6B, respectively, or alternatively in operative association with a frame member of the seat cushion 2.

Each of the first slide member 18A and the second slide member 18B preferably comprises an elongate track or rail member defining a slide path along which a corresponding follower portion of the associated support leg 6A, 6B, or of a bracket connected to the seat cushion 2, is configured to travel. The first slide member 18A and second slide member 18B are preferably disposed in a laterally spaced, generally parallel relationship relative to one another, so as to provide balanced support to the seat cushion 2 during displacement thereof.

In operation, as the seat cushion 2 is displaced from the first position toward the second position, a follower portion associated with each of the first support leg 6A and second support leg 6B travels along the slide path defined by the respective first slide member 18A and second slide member 18B, thereby permitting the forward portion of the seat cushion 2 to be raised while the first support leg 6A and second support leg 6B remain in engagement with, or in proximity to, the vehicle floor F. The slide mechanism 18A, 18B thereby cooperates with the leg holding member 8 and the third support leg 6C to permit smooth, controlled tilting movement of the seat cushion 2 without imparting undue stress upon the support legs 6A, 6B, 6C or upon the mounting structures associated therewith.

The first slide member 18A and second slide member 18B may further be provided with a stop portion or detent disposed at an end thereof, the stop portion being configured to limit travel of the corresponding follower portion, thereby defining the second position of the seat cushion 2 and preventing over-travel of the seat cushion 2 beyond a predetermined tilt angle.

### Operation

In use, an occupant or operator desiring to access the storage compartment S grasps a forward or intermediate portion of the seat cushion 2 and applies an upward force thereto. As the seat cushion 2 begins to pivot or displace about its rearward mounting region, the follower portions associated with the first support leg 6A and second support leg 6B travel along the respective first slide member 18A and second slide member 18B, while the third support leg 6C is guided by the leg holding member 8, whether by sliding displacement, rotational displacement, or a combination thereof.

Continued upward displacement of the seat cushion 2 causes the seat cushion 2 to reach the second position, in which the lower surface 2b of the seat cushion 2 is disposed at an angle relative to the vehicle floor F sufficient to expose the storage compartment S therebeneath, thereby permitting access to articles stored therein. The support legs 6A, 6B, 6C remain in engagement with, or in close proximity to, the vehicle floor F throughout the transition, thereby providing continued structural support to the seat assembly 1 and preventing collapse or instability of the seat cushion 2 in the second position.

To return the seat cushion 2 to the first, seating position, the occupant or operator applies a downward force to the seat cushion 2, causing the follower portions to travel in the reverse direction along the first slide member 18A and second slide member 18B, and causing the third support leg 6C to be guided back into its predetermined orientation by the leg holding member 8, until the seat cushion 2 returns to the first position, in which the upper surface 2a of the seat cushion 2 is again disposed to receive an occupant thereon.

## ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION

The vehicle seat assembly of the present invention provides a robust and reliable construction for accessing a storage compartment disposed beneath a seat cushion, while maintaining structural support of the seat cushion through the cooperative action of the support legs 6A, 6B, 6C, the leg holding member 8, and the slide mechanism 18A, 18B. The invention thereby overcomes the shortcomings of conventional seat storage arrangements by providing enhanced stability, ease of operation, and durability over repeated cycles of use.

   a slide mechanism comprising a first slide member and a second slide member, operatively associated with the first support leg and the second support leg, respectively, and configured to guide displacement of the first support leg and the second support leg upon movement of the seat cushion between the first position and the second position.

# TECHNICAL SUMMARY

## Field of the Invention

The present disclosure relates to vehicle seat mechanisms, and more particularly to a seat cushion tip-up mechanism configured to pivot a seat cushion forward such that a seating surface thereof faces a seat back, wherein a leg holding member is disposed on a sliding component of the mechanism.

## Background

Vehicle seating assemblies commonly employ tip-up or fold-flat mechanisms to increase cargo space or facilitate access to a vehicle floor region beneath the seat. Conventional tip-up mechanisms typically pivot the seat cushion about a fixed pivot axis located at a forward or rearward edge of the seat cushion frame. However, such fixed-axis arrangements may result in interference between the seat cushion and adjacent vehicle structures, such as a seat back or console, during the tip-up operation, and may further fail to accommodate variation in leg positioning of support linkages during the folding sequence.

## Summary of the Invention

According to an embodiment, a seat cushion tip-up mechanism is provided, comprising:

- a seat cushion frame supporting a seat cushion having a seating surface;
- a link mechanism connecting the seat cushion frame to a vehicle floor structure, the link mechanism including at least one leg member extending between the vehicle floor structure and the seat cushion frame;
- a sliding member movably coupled to the seat cushion frame or an associated bracket, the sliding member being configured to translate along a slide path defined relative to the seat cushion frame during a tip-up operation; and
- a leg holding member disposed on the sliding member, the leg holding member being configured to engage and retain a lower end portion of the leg member such that, as the sliding member translates along the slide path, the leg member is guided in coordinated movement with the seat cushion frame.

In operation, actuation of the tip-up mechanism causes the seat cushion frame to pivot forward about a pivot axis such that the seating surface, normally oriented upward for occupant seating, is rotated to face rearward toward the seat back. Simultaneously, the sliding member translates along the slide path, and the leg holding member carried thereon guides the leg member of the link mechanism, thereby coordinating collapse or repositioning of the leg member with the pivoting motion of the seat cushion frame. This coordinated movement enables the seat cushion to fold compactly against or adjacent to the seat back while avoiding interference between the link mechanism and surrounding vehicle structure.

## Advantageous Effects

The disclosed configuration provides several advantages over conventional arrangements:

1. **Coordinated Kinematics** — By positioning the leg holding member on the sliding component, the mechanism achieves synchronized movement between cushion rotation and leg member displacement, reducing the risk of mechanical interference during the tip-up stroke.

2. **Compact Folded Profile** — The forward tip-up motion, combined with controlled leg guidance, permits the seat cushion to nest more closely against the seat back, thereby maximizing available cargo or floor space.

3. **Reduced Component Stress** — Guided translation of the leg member via the leg holding member distributes operational loads more evenly across the link mechanism, potentially reducing wear at pivot joints.

4. **Simplified Actuation** — The integration of the leg holding member directly onto the sliding member allows a single actuation input (e.g., manual lever or motor-driven linkage) to simultaneously drive both the tip-up rotation and the leg-guiding translation, reducing the number of independent components required for operation.

## Brief Description of Representative Embodiments

In one representative embodiment, the sliding member comprises a slide plate or slide bracket mounted for reciprocal linear movement along a rail or track fixed to the seat cushion frame. The leg holding member may be configured as a hook, slot, bracket, or clip formed integrally with or attached to the sliding member, dimensioned to receivably engage a pin, roller, or end portion of the leg member.

In another embodiment, the link mechanism may comprise a four-bar linkage or multi-bar linkage arrangement, wherein the leg member constitutes one link of the linkage, and wherein displacement of the sliding member effects a corresponding angular or translational displacement of the leg member relative to the vehicle floor structure.

Additional embodiments may incorporate biasing members (e.g., springs) to urge the sliding member toward a stowed or deployed position, and/or locking mechanisms configured to selectively retain the seat cushion frame in either a normal seating position or a tipped-up storage position.

## Industrial Applicability

The described seat cushion tip-up mechanism is applicable to a wide range of vehicle seating systems, including but not limited to second-row and third-row seating assemblies in passenger vehicles, where forward tip-up folding is desired to expand cargo capacity or provide floor access, while maintaining reliable coordination between the seat cushion and its associated support linkage.

# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a foldable car seat cushion system configured to maximize available storage space within a vehicle interior when the seat is not in use for seating purposes, while providing stable, comfortable support during normal seating operation.

In one aspect, the invention provides a seat cushion assembly comprising a cushion body, at least one pair of support legs (10) pivotally connected to a lower portion of the cushion body, and a leg holder (20) configured to receive and retain the support legs (10) in a folded, storage-ready configuration. The support legs (10) are movable between an extended position, in which the legs (10) support the cushion body at a raised height suitable for seating, and a retracted position, in which the legs (10) are folded substantially flush against or beneath the cushion body and secured by the leg holder (20), thereby reducing the overall vertical profile of the seat assembly.

In a further aspect, the seat cushion system includes a slide rail assembly (30) mounted to a floor structure of the vehicle, the slide rail assembly (30) comprising one or more slide rails (32) engaging corresponding sliding members disposed on an underside of the cushion body or support leg assembly. The slide rails (32) permit the entire seat cushion assembly to be translated along a longitudinal or lateral axis of the vehicle, allowing the seat to be moved into a stowed position adjacent a sidewall, rear panel, or beneath an adjoining seat structure, independent of or in combination with the folding operation of the support legs (10).

According to the invention, the leg holder (20) is disposed at a predetermined location on the underside of the cushion body or on an adjacent structural frame, and is configured with a receiving channel, clip, or latch mechanism dimensioned to engage a distal end of each support leg (10) when the legs (10) are pivoted into the folded position. This engagement secures the support legs (10) against unwanted movement during transport or storage, and prevents rattling, shifting, or accidental deployment of the legs (10) while the seat cushion is in its collapsed configuration.

The combination of the pivotable support legs (10), the cooperating leg holder (20), and the slide rail (30) assembly enables the seat cushion system to transition between a fully deployed seating configuration and a compact, low-profile stowed configuration, in which the folded support legs (10) are secured by the leg holder (20) and the entire assembly may be slid along the slide rails (32) to a storage-optimized position. This arrangement significantly increases usable cargo or floor space within the vehicle when the seat is not occupied, while maintaining structural stability, ease of deployment, and durability of the seat cushion assembly during normal use.

In accordance with further embodiments, the support legs (10) may be provided with locking mechanisms to secure them in the extended position, the leg holder (20) may include resilient or spring-biased elements to facilitate quick-release engagement and disengagement of the support legs (10), and the slide rails (32) may incorporate detent or lock positions to secure the seat cushion assembly at one or more predetermined locations along the rail path. These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become apparent from the following detailed description, accompanying drawings, and appended claims.
